data.name: Spartan VR
data.detailed_description:
With your shield or on it!

Gameplay features

  • An exciting adventure you will never forget!
  • Epic, brutal and immersive melee combat!
  • Block, parry, stab, slice, throw spear and use magic!
  • Put on the Sandals of Hermes and fly like a bird!
  • Explore an awesome ancient world in VR with your HTC Vive or Oculus Rift!

Story


Are you ready to become a Spartan in the world of Ancient Greece? Have you ever wanted to feel what it's like to be in the shoes of legendary Greek heroes? Spartan VR beckons you to rise to the challenge, sharpen your spears and fight to the end!

Waking up in the hold of your own ship in shackles and armed with magical artifacts of Hermes, you will under his patronage undergo a series of tests and save the little that survived in the battle of the Titans.

data.short_description: Built exclusively for VR. The game puts you in the midst of ancient Greek myths! Become a true Greek hero and fight in real time with swords, shields and spears against legendary Hades's creatures!

Mínimos:

  • Memória: 16 GB de RAM

  • DirectX: Versão 10
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 7 GB de espaço livre
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR or Oculus PC. Standing or Room Scale

reviews.review:
Spartan VR is a virtual reality action game built around the fantasy of becoming a warrior in a world inspired by Ancient Greek mythology. Developed and published by Immergity, it was created specifically for VR and places physical interaction at the center of the experience. Instead of relying on conventional button-driven combat, players swing weapons, defend themselves with a shield, throw spears, and use supernatural abilities through motion controls. It is an ambitious concept, especially considering its 2017 origins, although the final experience feels more like a compact showcase of early VR combat ideas than a fully developed mythological epic.

The adventure begins with the player awakening in chains aboard a ship before becoming connected to Hermes and his magical artifacts. From there, the story provides an excuse to travel through mythological environments, complete trials, and battle various enemies. The narrative is relatively straightforward and does not attempt the elaborate storytelling or character development of a traditional role-playing game. Instead, Greek mythology supplies the atmosphere and gives context to the weapons, powers, creatures, and locations encountered throughout the campaign.

Melee combat is the main attraction. Swords can be physically swung and thrust toward opponents, while shields allow players to protect themselves against incoming attacks. Spears introduce a ranged option because they can be thrown, and magical powers add another layer beyond ordinary weapon fighting. There is satisfaction in successfully defending against an enemy before immediately retaliating with a physical strike. The system is accessible enough to understand quickly, but it also encourages players to move their bodies rather than simply stand still and press controller buttons.

One of the more memorable mechanics involves the Sandals of Hermes, which provide the ability to fly. Movement through the air complements the supernatural theme and gives the game an identity beyond being another VR sword-fighting arena. Combining aerial movement with conventional weapons and magical abilities creates moments where Spartan VR delivers the heroic power fantasy promised by its setting. There is considerable imagination behind these mechanics even when their implementation does not always have the polish necessary to make them completely convincing.

Its age becomes much more apparent in the overall presentation. Character animations, environmental detail, enemy behavior, and physical interactions are noticeably simpler than those found in newer VR titles. Combat can become repetitive once the novelty of physically swinging weapons begins to fade, while encounters do not always provide enough tactical variety to sustain the concept over extended sessions. The environments establish an appropriate mythological atmosphere but generally lack the density and interactivity that modern VR players may expect.

The game's history as an Early Access project is also important when setting expectations. Its foundation contains several promising concepts, including multiple locations, arena-style combat, different weapons, magic, and unusual traversal mechanics. However, the experience retains the feeling of a project whose ideas were larger than its eventual scope. There is enjoyable material here, but players expecting a substantial campaign filled with exploration, progression systems, sophisticated physics, and numerous enemy types are likely to find it limited.

Spartan VR was designed for PC virtual reality hardware and requires tracked VR controllers for its core interactions. Standing and room-scale play fit the physical nature of the combat particularly well. The hardware requirements are modest compared with current PC standards, but owning an appropriate PC VR headset and controller setup remains essential. Steam Deck compatibility should therefore be considered unsupported for practical purposes. The Steam Deck itself cannot provide the tracked VR headset and motion-controller environment the game requires, so this is not a title intended for normal handheld Deck play.

Additional features include Steam achievements, statistics, and leaderboards, giving completion-focused players some extra objectives beyond simply finishing encounters. Multiple interface languages are available, while English also receives broader audio and subtitle support. These features are welcome, although they remain secondary to the physical VR combat that defines the entire experience.

Spartan VR works best when approached as a product of the earlier period of consumer virtual reality. Its greatest strength is the immediate pleasure of stepping into a mythological warrior fantasy, raising a shield, swinging a sword, hurling a spear, using magical abilities, and eventually taking flight. Its weaknesses come from limited depth, dated visuals, repetitive encounters, and an overall lack of refinement compared with later VR action games. The underlying ideas are often more impressive than their execution.

For players fascinated by Greek mythology or curious about older PC VR experiments, there is still some entertainment to discover. The combination of physical melee combat and supernatural abilities gives it personality, and flying with the powers of Hermes remains an interesting addition. It simply never develops those ingredients into the expansive adventure they could have supported. As a short VR curiosity it has charm, but as a complete action-adventure it leaves considerable room for improvement.

Rating: 6/10
